turns.prompt: Now write me a Python function. Put it in a single fenced code block tagged as python. It should define `def fizzbuzz(n: int) -> list[str]:` returning the FizzBuzz strings for 1..n, and below the function include a line that prints fizzbuzz(15). The code must run as-is under python3 with no edits and no imports of anything unavailable.
In AT MOST 15 words, explain why binary search is faster than linear search. Do not exceed 15 words.
turns.answer: Binary search halves the search space each step; linear search checks items one by one.

turns.prompt: Explain the time complexity of binary search and state the recurrence, using inline LaTeX mathematics delimited with dollar signs (like $O(\log n)$) rather than plain text notation. Two short paragraphs.
turns.answer:
Binary search runs in $O(\log n)$ time because each comparison halves the remaining search space.

Its recurrence is $T(n)=T(n/2)+O(1)$, which solves to $T(n)=O(\log n)$.

turns.prompt: Reponds entierement en francais, sans un seul mot d'anglais: explique en trois phrases ce qu'est une table de hachage et pourquoi ses recherches sont rapides.
turns.answer:
Une table de hachage associe des clés à des valeurs grâce à une fonction de hachage.  
Cette fonction transforme chaque clé en un emplacement où trouver la valeur.  
Les recherches sont rapides car elles vont presque directement au bon emplacement.
